summary.headline: Indo Count Q2 FY27 total income rose 57% YoY to INR1,699 crore and EBITDA margin hit 15.3%, with H1 margin 14.4% above the 13% full-year guidance.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarter, with total income of INR1,699 crore (up 57% YoY, 39% QoQ) and EBITDA more than doubling to INR259 crore. PAT rose to INR132 crore from INR39 crore. Net debt fell to INR518 crore, the lowest level, and net debt to equity was 0.2x. Management said it expects to exceed FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance, but did not raise the numeric guidance, and reiterated the CY28 revenue target of INR8,000 crore.

segments.name: Core bed linen
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR2,033 crore, about 50% of the INR4,000 crore FY27 target. Core EBITDA is above the ~15% guided level; about 70% of core revenue is US and 30% non-US.

segments.name: New businesses (utility bedding, branded, other home textiles)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR502 crore (~30% of total income); H1 revenue INR890 crore, nearly 60% of the INR1,500 crore FY27 target. Mix is roughly two-thirds utility bedding and one-third branded. EBITDA margin is in the low double digits, below core, and is expected to reach core levels (~15%) at full utilisation.

segments.name: US utility bedding plants
segments.commentary: All three US facilities have ramped up and are running at over 65% utilisation, with management saying all three are above 65%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance of 105-110 million meters volume, INR5,500 crore total income and 13% EBITDA margin: management expects to exceed both the revenue and EBITDA guidance. H1 delivered 51 million meters (~49% of volume guidance) and INR2,923 crore (~53% of revenue guidance).
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance may move from 13% to 14-15%, but management said it will not go beyond that. It declined to change guidance to 18-20%.

CY28 target of doubling revenue from FY25 to INR8,000 crore (branded business target $100 million by CY28); management reiterated this and said it does not need growth capex to reach it. Management will provide next-year guidance later.
Non-US core revenue is expected to grow over 20% in FY27; the non-US share of core could move from about 30% toward 40-50% over the next few years, though management gave no firm number.

FY27 capex guidance of INR250 crore is to be spent over 12-18 months, with about INR40 crore spent in H1; the full amount will not be spent this year. Spinning capex is mostly expected by year-end, and effluent treatment will likely spill into FY28.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance of INR250 crore over 12-18 months; about INR40 crore spent in H1 FY27.
Projects: spinning (mostly expected to complete before FY27 year-end) and effluent treatment plant (likely to spill over into FY28).

Core business utilisation is about 73%, with some spare capacity; board to decide on further capex at an appropriate time. Management said no growth capex is needed to reach the CY28 INR8,000 crore target.
All three US utility bedding plants above 65% utilisation; management targets full utilisation of the utility business by CY28.
demand_pricing: Average realisation rose sharply, which management attributed to higher-value orders executed this quarter and product mix; management said the mix is sustainable. Refunds of US tariffs are not included in the realisation gain.
Gross margin is expected to range 50-55% on an annualised basis and should not be judged quarter by quarter, due to product mix.

Cotton and cotton-related input costs have risen; the company holds 4-5 months of inventory as a cushion and passes on increases with a lag of one to two quarters. Management said the previous input cost increase has been fully passed on and sees no margin pressure.
Freight is largely on FOB or CIF terms, so customers bear freight hikes.
UK FTA implemented in July 2026; EU FTA not yet effective. Customer inquiries are rising in the UK and EU, and management said the UK and EU addressable opportunity is comparable to the US.
Wamsutta expanded into broader US retail, and was a major driver of branded growth. Growth came from both market share gains and wallet share gains with existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Do margins already reflect rising input costs, or is there downside ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cotton inputs are covered by 4-5 months of inventory and price increases are passed on with a one-to-two-quarter lag, so no margin pressure is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company double its size from FY27 to FY30 and reach INR10,000 crore at 20% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it stays with the CY28 guidance of doubling revenue from FY25 to INR8,000 crore and will give next-year guidance later. It said it will work towards more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin gap between core and new businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Core EBITDA is about 15% and above that in Q2. New businesses are in the low double digits and should reach core levels within the next two to three quarters, with full utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Has US core volume recovered to FY25 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY25 volume was about 106 million meters and FY27 is heading to roughly the same level, with US and non-US combined to recover the base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital rise in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the working capital cycle improved from March, with the number of days down by at least three weeks as of 30 September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 capex of INR250 crore be fully spent this year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The INR250 crore is over 12-18 months; about INR40 crore was spent in H1, with spinning mostly done this year and effluent treatment spilling into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Could margin guidance move to 18-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Not immediately. The FY27 margin could go from 13% to 14-15%, but management said it will not go beyond that.

risks_watch: US demand and operating environment after the midterm elections; management declined to comment on the results and said the order book is healthy.
Input cost (cotton and yarn) inflation and the timing of pass-through to customers.
New business margins are still in the low double digits; reaching the ~15% core level depends on utilisation and the branded mix.
Bhilad flood: final insurance settlement is pending (interim INR14 crore 99 lakh received approval); the INR45 crore inventory loss is offset as an exceptional item.
Dependence on US volumes: the non-US share of core is only about 30% today, and EU FTA timing is uncertain.
Management gave no numeric guidance beyond FY27 and CY28, and no split of the remaining capex between H2 FY27 and FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on near-term delivery: management said it will beat FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance and repeated the CY28 target. It was cautious on numeric upgrades, holding guidance and limiting the margin raise to 14-15%. It deflected or declined on several specifics, including the midterm election impact, the non-US mix, the capex split, and the cost bridge.

Overall, the blended margin for this year, we have guided it, given in 13%. Overall, we should be exceeding that.
The full INR250 crores will not be spent during this year.
Gross margin should be looked at on annual basis. Do not go with quarter- by- quarter.
